# TwoSum on values of the program

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `two_sum_entry` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

$a + b$, exactly:

$$s + e = a + b.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `two_sum(a, b)` | `T`, `T` | `SumAndError<T>` | `constexpr`, with the same values in constant evaluation (a zero result can differ in sign); rounds; the operands are guarded ([rule R3](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)); `r.sum` is $s$ and `r.error` is $e$; `Expansion<T, 2>(r)` is the pair as a number, canonical when both are finite: for finite $a$, $b$ whose sum does not overflow and $\lvert b\rvert < \Omega$ (with $b = \pm\Omega$ the error term can be a NaN although the sum is finite) |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $s = \mathrm{RN}(a + b)$.
- $s + e = a + b$ exactly.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `two_sum_entry_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/EntryKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/EntryKernels.v), against `two_sum_entry_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions two_sum_entry_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition two_sum_entry_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a b : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec b ->
  let '(s, e) := two_sum_entry emin prec tie_even a b in
  fmt emin prec s /\
  fmt emin prec e /\
  s = RN emin prec (a + b) /\
  (s + e) = (a + b).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `two_sum_entry_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** TwoSum (Knuth, TAOCP vol. 2, 4.2.2; Moller 1965) on its guarded operands (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/two_sum_entry.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/two_sum_entry.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`two_sum`](two_sum.md).

```
# two_sum for the public building block kairn::two_sum (milestone2.md, "Values that enter from the
# program"): both operands pass through guard, then two_sum. The program may pass a product, which
# a contracting compiler would otherwise fuse into the first addition, so that the error term
# would be computed from a sum that is not RN(a + b). guard(a) has the value of a: the statement
# is two_sum's. Not claimed: the sign of a zero result, which the guard can change.

ga     = guard(a)
gb     = guard(b)
(s, e) = two_sum(ga, gb)
```

## Measured

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
